title: Or with a friend
hookLine: in the middle of the rhinoceros poem, a door opens: if you find a wise companion, walk with them
carry: we praise the blessing of companionship

cards: Verse after verse, the rhinoceros poem ends the same way: wander alone. Read it fast and you'd think the whole message is: don't need anyone. But look near the start.
Two verses sit side by side, and they don't end the way the others do. They start with the word if. If you find someone.
It's like a long letter from a friend who keeps saying I'm fine on my own, I'm fine on my own, and then, partway down the page, writes: unless you'd like to come.

teach.h: IF YOU FIND A WISE COMPANION
teach.b: Roughly, the verse says: if you find a wise companion, a fellow traveler who lives well and is steady, walk with them, overcoming every danger, glad and mindful.
And the next: if you don't find one like that, walk alone, like a king who has left a conquered kingdom behind, like an elephant alone in the forest. So solitude was never the goal.
It's what you do when the right companion isn't there. The poem even says what makes a companion right. Wise: the Pali word is nipaka, skilled, discerning.
Living well. Steady. Someone who makes the dangers smaller, not bigger.
A little later comes a line like a proverb: we praise the blessing of companionship. Keep company with those better than you or equal to you. If you can't find them, live blamelessly and walk alone.
Elsewhere in the discourses, Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, says: good friendship is half of the spiritual life. And the Buddha corrects him: don't say that, Ananda.

teach.h: FRIENDSHIP IS THE WHOLE OF IT
teach.b: Good friendship is the whole of the spiritual life.
So the tradition holds both, the one horn and the good friend. Not a contradiction: two pictures of the same freedom. You don't need a crowd.
And when someone wise and kind turns up on your road, you don't need to walk alone either.

how: Buddhist teaching speaks of the kalyanamitta, the good or noble friend, and Buddhists practice in groups, with a teacher, or with a trusted companion, alongside times of solitude.

o: a companion, a friend to walk the road with
the head monk of a large forest monastery
a rival who tests your patience

games.q: the rhinoceros poem turns: tap the pairs.
p: if you find a wise companion
walk with them, glad and mindful
walk alone, like an elephant in the forest
the whole of the spiritual life

s: the rhinoceros poem says never to travel with anyone
two verses in the middle say: if you find a wise companion, walk with them.
Ananda said good friendship is half the spiritual life
and the Buddha corrected him: it's the whole of it.
the poem says to keep company with those better than you or equal to you
and if you can't find them, to live blamelessly and walk alone.

games.q: you're Ananda. you've been thinking about friendship and say: good friends are half of the spiritual life. what does the Buddha say?
o: don't say that: it's the whole of it.
games.why: in the discourse called Half, the Buddha tells Ananda that good friendship is the whole of the spiritual life.

practice: Bring to mind someone who makes the road safer, wise, steady and kind, near or far or no longer living, and picture walking beside them, matching steps, not talking much.
If there's no one like that right now, picture the friend you'd like to find, and the friend you'd like to be, and rest in that company.

wordCard.voice: sahaya. The turn in the rhinoceros poem: if you find a wise and steady companion, walk with them, glad and mindful. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali sahaya: companion, friend. the rhinoceros poem's wise companion is a nipaka sahaya.

carryVoice: Your line: we praise the blessing of companionship. The one horn and the good friend, both. Day five hundred eighty, done.
